newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Kiguel says no decision on Moody's.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Kiguel says no decision on Moody's.

text.p: Argentine Undersecretary of Finance Miguel Kiguel said Tuesday officials have not given thought to the idea of terminating its ratings contract with Moody's Investors Corp but were talking to the IBCA agency.

"We have not thought about it. We have neither thought of terminating the contract nor of extending it," Kiguel told journalists, when asked about a Clarin newspaper report saying the ministry is going to end its contract with Moody's.
"The contract (with Moody's) runs out in October so we have lots of time to think about it," he added.
However, asked about whether he disagreed with Moody's B1 foreign currency rating of Argentina he said: "Definitely. You can say that in every way."
Asked about IBCA, the European rating agency, he responded: "We are talking to IBCA."
The Clarin article, published Monday, said Argentina was going to drop its deal with Moody's in favor of IBCA.
"The relationship (with Moody's) is good but we have strong differences on how to evaluate Argentine risk," added the official.
Last year Argentina announced it was going to make a greater effort in working to raise its credit-ratings from major international raters.

Standard & Poor's raised Argentina's sovereign rating recently but Moody's has so far given no indication it intends to do the same because of Argentina's high level of foreign debt as a proportion of exports.
